page: Amazon Web Services r8idn.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core. There are no GPUs equipped on this configuration.

Storage architecture incorporates 237 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage. For network connectivity, the instance provides a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps. Public IPv4 addresses are not included complimentary with this allocation. The local NVMe drive delivers low-latency scratch storage, though instance store volumes are ephemeral and require external replication or snapshotting strategies to prevent data loss upon instance termination or stop operations.

From an efficiency standpoint, the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio offers a dense memory configuration combined with local high-speed disk resources. While standard EBS-only instances may lower baseline infrastructure spend for stateless services, the inclusion of direct-attached NVMe and a 3.9 GHz processor provides hardware consolidation for I/O-intensive workloads. Appropriate use cases include in-memory caching systems, transactional databases requiring high-speed local scratch disks, real-time analytics, and data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idn.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It utilizes a 3.9 GHz x86_64 Intel processor providing 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, accompanied by 32.0 GB of RAM. The instance includes 237 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and supports a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. No graphics processing units are present in this configuration. The 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio, paired with onboard ephemeral NVMe storage, balances fast memory retrieval with local drive throughput. This configuration targets resource profiles requiring high memory density alongside fast temporary storage, including in-memory datastores, relational database engines, real-time caching, and distributed data analysis workflows.
